name: AXM Native Learning Shell
notes: Runs Mirror's inspectable bounded learning route, including real episodic capture, typed contract-derived private exams with a stable held-out module split, proposal-only manifest-bound exact typed handoff graph routing at depth one and two, a separate typed dynamic Technical Glasses readiness overlay, automatic reviewable nonbuilt missing-probe hand planning, automatic provider-declaration research-exam planning, a bounded read-only per-document provider-declaration architecture pattern survey, a following bounded static JavaScript implementation-evidence survey, and a balanced exported-source by positive-UNTESTED-hypothesis provider-binding experiment matrix whose frames remain unselected. Explicit reviewed provider-declaration research-executor and readiness-probe-candidate batches remain empty because this automatic route has no human-review authority. It also runs parent-linked synthetic counterexamples, evaluation-only atomic and generated depth-two metamorphic invariance probes, and known-fail evidence exclusion. Generated contract wording is non-authoritative; held-out contract exams, handoff route matches, readiness classifications and false-ready decoys, research-exam requests, pattern assessments, selector-source assessments, binding-experiment frames, executor fixture receipts, readiness hand requests, candidate build receipts, unbound route decoys, and confirmed invariants do not become training examples. It does not execute surveyed source, merge declaration relations across documents, infer a provider identity or outer requirement binding from patterns or selector literals, copy consumer permissions into a provider, select a binding frame or implementation by ordering or frequency, infer or approve a research-executor or probe recipe, select or evaluate a provider architecture automatically, generate provider or readiness candidate code automatically, install or run a probe live, execute routed modules, start or repair readiness, expose hidden chain-of-thought, or promote runtime, semantic truth, canon, identity, permissions, or tools.
